I call Lisa, explain what I presented to the board, and ask if she would be willing to mention the pipeline as a potential pathway when she is working with displaced workers who have a mechanical or technical background.

Continue teaching current auto shop curriculum while awaiting the board decision. No reactive curriculum changes, no premature pivots. The program as it exists is still operating. I teach this week's classes with the same quality and engagement I always bring. I do not treat the pending board decision as a reason to deprioritize the students in front of me.
auto_shop_teacher.inner_monologue: I put everything I had into that presentation — nine ticks of evidence, a real industry partner, a councilmember's endorsement. Now the board has it. I cannot force the decision and I would not want to. What I can do is make sure the pieces around the decision keep moving: keep Sarah committed, get Lisa routing people to the pipeline, find out when the vote is happening. If the board approves this, Millfield gets a technician pipeline for the exact vehicles now driving through its streets. If they do not, I need to know quickly enough to figure out what comes next. But I am not going to that contingency yet. I believe in this proposal.

community_organizer.name: Lisa Freeman
actions: Launch the Financial Triage Navigator function at the community center. Not as a pilot — as an operating service that begins this week. The structure: Tuesday and Thursday evenings during community connection night, a trained volunteer (I will start as the volunteer) sits with a community member for 45 minutes. The session covers: current income and expense picture, what programs they have already applied for and what the status is, what programs they qualify for but have not applied to, and a specific prioritized list of three next steps with contact information attached. I am not a financial planner. I am a person who knows what resources exist in Millfield and can map them to a person's actual situation in plain language. I start doing this this week.

Call Angela Wright directly — before this week's community connection night — to coordinate intake. Angela is processing displaced Hawkins workers by phone call this week. I tell her: when you finish the intake call, if the worker does not have a next step that is already defined and specific, tell them to come to the community center Tuesday or Thursday evening. We run a 45-minute session that produces a prioritized action list. Give them my name and tell them to ask for me. I am not trying to own the relationship. I am adding a step in the pipeline that Angela's intake process does not have time to cover.

Respond to Dorothy Chen's proposal about expanding transportation sessions into a broader 'economic transition for older adults' workshop series. I tell her yes — with conditions. Yes, I will give her a time slot and a platform at the community center. The condition: she brings the curriculum draft to me before the first session and we review it together to ensure it covers the financial decision dimension, not just the transportation dimension. Older adults facing asset decisions — whether to sell a car, how to evaluate RoboRide for their specific mobility needs, how to access fixed-income programs if their expenses spike — need more than transportation navigation. They need the economic framing too. Dorothy has the credibility with that demographic. I have the framework. Together we build something real.

Host this week's Community Connection Night with a deliberate structure that acknowledges the current moment directly. Opening segment: I name the Hawkins closure, the protests, and the employment numbers out loud — not to alarm people, but to validate what everyone in the room already knows. People who come to a community center in a crisis do not want to be managed around the crisis. They want to be seen. I name it in two sentences, acknowledge it is real and hard, and then move to the tools: the Financial Triage Navigator is now operating here, tonight, and going forward. If you need it, I am here.
community_organizer.inner_monologue: Nine ticks of watching people come through this door looking lost, and now I am finally in the room where some of the decisions are being made. That Financial Triage Navigator concept brief was not just a policy document — it was me telling the council: I know what people need and I am going to provide it with or without your endorsement. I do not need their blessing to start. I start Tuesday. The anger I carry about how slow the institutions have been is not going to paralyze me. I am going to use it to move faster.

uber_driver_2.name: Grace Okafor
actions: Call Millfield Medical Transport and CareRide of the Valley this week — the same operators Robert named. I have the NEMT certification in hand. I lead with that fact and state my availability clearly: I am certified, I have a clean driving record, I have a vehicle that meets commercial standards, and I can start within the week. I ask one direct question: is there an onboarding slot available and when can I schedule an interview or orientation? I do not wait for Robert's offer to confirm before calling. I act on his intelligence directly. If Robert has already spoken to these operators, I mention his name — not to piggyback on his application, but to establish that I come from the same credible pipeline he does.

Drive every available high-yield shift this week. Morning airport windows (5am-9am), Friday evening surge block, Saturday morning airport window. Also drive Tuesday and Wednesday afternoon if demand holds above minimum threshold. I am not being selective anymore — I am maximizing hours within the constraint of clinical study commitments. Target: $800-900 in rideshare income this tick. That is not enough to fully cover $1,787 in expenses, but it is the difference between two weeks of partial runway and complete collapse.

Send a brief, direct update to Robert Jackson. One paragraph: I received his message and I am acting on it. I am calling the operators this week with the cert in hand. I mention that I am using his name as a credibility reference — not to freeload on his pipeline, but to establish shared network context. I ask one thing: if either Millfield Medical Transport or CareRide gives him an offer this week, can he tell me the name of the contact person he spoke to? That specific warm introduction — even a name — cuts through the cold call queue. I ask for it directly because he offered to give it and I should not be too proud to accept.

Send a brief, warm thank-you to Denise Williams acknowledging her note. One sentence of gratitude, one sentence of update: the cert is done and I am calling operators this week. I note her intelligence about the Millfield General step-down unit expansion — tell her I am filing that for the medium-term nursing trajectory and that she may be inside the institution where I eventually work. I do not ask her for anything. I keep the relationship alive because it is worth keeping alive.
uber_driver_2.inner_monologue: Sixty-eight dollars. I have driven more miles than I can count in this city and I am down to sixty-eight dollars. I am not panicking because panic is useless — but I am scared in the honest way, the way that makes you move. The cert is real. The operators are real. Robert's intelligence is good and I trust it. I call today, I drive this week, and I do not stop until one of those two things produces income. I did not come this far through nursing school to fold when the plan hits friction. I adapt. That is what I do.
